steps.name: Villager
steps.text: This way! Over here!

steps.name: Villager
steps.text: Ugh, help me nail that door shut! Hold it steady!

steps.name: Villager
steps.text: Has anyone seen our third oldest? We're missing a child.

steps.name: Villager
steps.text: Ha—Have you seen Yü anywhere?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Apologies, I have never seen them...

steps.name: Villager
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: Villager
steps.text: Oh, Yü, little Yü, where are you...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Here, I'll buy you some sweeties. How about that?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Shall I take you to see the fireworks?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: ...If your mama was here, little Ah Jan, she wouldn't want to see you refusing to eat or drink, would she?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Mama... mamaaaaa...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Oh. Cry, cry it out, now. Better than keeping it all trapped inside.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Mr. Nothing, who's this child?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Oh, benefactor... this child is called Ah Jan. I heard her father left home in search of work so long ago, and never came back. She hasn't seen her mother since yesterday, and has been utterly shaken ever since. She still hasn't had a single thing to eat or drink, not even today...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Benefactor! My benefactor, don't look so downcast. If it weren't for you and Kroos, this village's people would be suffering so terribly. As the proverb puts it...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: ...Oh, what use would be a proverb.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Benefactor, what do we do now?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Find Dawn and that storyteller.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: They clearly know something.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: Oh... a rare guest.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Do you recognize me?

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: Owner of the Elegant Garden, the Umbrella-Boiler. In P'o-shan Village, who doesn't know of you?

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: The storyteller you are, inheritor of that great merchant's gardens, you're the very god of P'o-shan Village.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: Please sit, sir.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: ...I refrain.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: You're already leaving?

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: You're very strangely silent today... that said, stay for the moment, please.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: Usually, it's you telling everyone stories to relieve the boredom, and all you take is some token money for tea.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: How about today, instead, I tell you a story? And I won't take any tips; this bowl of tea is free. How about it, sir?

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: Today, the story I'll tell will be much simpler than any of those mythical tales you've collected.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: They say that ten years ago, on the southeast border of Yan, there was a small town named P'o-shan...

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: No. You can continue.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: Mm. Okay.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: P'o-shan was normal as could be. It had no more than a hundred households, and they lived off the mountain, passing simple days. Sometimes a merchant caravan would pass through, and on those days, the children went wild with joy.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: And this small town, one day, suffered a Catastrophe.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: The Catastrophe didn't completely destroy the town, but active Originium polluted its springs. The adults thought to seek aid from a nearby city, but there were no town Messengers, and all the adults who left went completely dark.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: So, helpless, the people abandoned this town, and began to aimlessly journey—

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: Nobody from the town actually knew where to go, and they didn't even have an idea of where the nearest city was. It was just as if they entrusted themselves to fate, and chose a direction.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: To the children, the warm beds, the winding fences, the amusing water stains along the walls, had all suddenly turned into pitch-black nights, and one... very long road.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: And on this road, many starved to death.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: There was a child, not very old, whose family was so poor.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: She went with her mother and father, watching as all her close neighbors had less and less to say.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: Watching as all the older kids who played with her fought each other, fought with sharp stones, over a moldy piece of shaobing bread.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: She thought, maybe things would get better. And she tried hard, to find berries, find small animals, catch the scalecis in the river.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: She almost drowned in there trying to catch them, and several times passed out from hunger.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: Maybe fortune felt cruel one day. Maybe the ones closest to her came to a sudden realization, that this thin little girl's final use would be to save them some rations.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: And when she returned 'home' clutching mountain fruits she didn't know if anyone could eat, there was not a single person left.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: The cry of the beasts on the cold night cliff reminded her: her life was worth nothing. In her confused daze, it was as if heaven and her were of the same sympathy, every inch of her skin telling her the temperature of death. And then—

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: She met someone. A... very strange someone.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: How did it go again? Oh... if you'd like to know what happened, you'll have to hear it next time.

steps.name: Dawn
steps.text: Leaving an audience hanging at these points is so rotten to do. How does it feel, sir, having the rare chance to taste it as an ordinary person?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Oh, shopkeep, I have been searching for thee for some while—

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: —Ho? Why art thou here, sir? In that great disaster just now, all were worrying for thee.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: No particular reason... only taking a stroll in here.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Saga.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Hm? I am here.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: You've been in the painting long. It is about time. This is enough now.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Why exhaust yourself catching the moon in the water?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: All are in stupor, you alone awake. Yet you act in a stupor still, and it pains to see.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Thou art not the storyteller... indeed, thou art...

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Fend for yourself.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: My compliments. To your fan.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Oh, dear, if it isn't my benefactor Kroos. What brings you barreling in?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: *Sigh* The people have all met calamity this time. No matter. I, along with you two benefactors, will help them rebuild this garden.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: ...Mr. Nothing.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Perhaps you really are just a normal Messenger, but I still need to warn you something...

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: The way things are, if you're still gonna keep holding stuff back from us... we're gonna have to give up our trust in you.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: ...My benefactor! What are you saying!?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: My compliments. To your fan.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: ...You saw that?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: I did.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: There's all kinds of martial arts, and I'm no specialist, but your skills aren't half bad... not half bad any way you slice 'em.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: I'm assuming you hide your skills for some personal reason or other. I'm not planning to dig out what it is...

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: ...but I do not like people when they a) clearly have the power to get in and help out, but b) find every excuse to play the coward.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Strictly speaking, that's selfish as hell, isn't it?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Eh, those might've been some harsh words, but you did save little Ah Jan too. Don't need to feel too guilty.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: I'm sorry, benefactor. You both saved me. I really ought to give you the whole story.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Perhaps, benefactor... you long since saw through me?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Course I did. Watching you put on the act was funny, that's all.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Ahahah... once we've gotten out of here, I'll give you two a full confession.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Then it's agreed.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Benefactor... I'm wondering about something.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: I'm wondering, before we suddenly saw the light in this garden, how long did we spend... trapped in this unusual village? I have absolutely no idea... that is to say...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Just how long has it been since we opened that door on Mount Hui-ch'i?
